newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar nudges higher, scores new highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar nudges higher, scores new highs.

text.p: Commission house buying kept London's October white sugar contract supported above $325.00 on Tuesday morning as the spot price scored another in a series of nine-month highs, traders said.
Solid buying from one leading player, thought to be for a fund, dominated the early part of the session.
Traders said there was also some French buying in the London market, probably pre-hedging in advance of the weekly European Union tender for sugar export licences.
October rallied to an intraday peak of $326.00, the highest since September 1996.
Technical analysts said short-term momentum indicators suggested the market's bullish sentiment remained intact, pegging nearby resistance at $329.00.
"The whites market looks well positioned to make further headway," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden. Support was well established at $321.70 followed by $320.00, he said.
At 1130 GMT October was up $1.10 at $325.80 and December up 20 cents at $320.40. Volume was concentrated in mainly outright October trades and totalled 648 lots.
The MATIF October contract showed the only price movement on the Paris market, up $1.00 at $325.00. Volume amounted to 210 lots. Nothing was traded on the lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA market.
